9.0.0.en: The children of Israel gathered of themselves out of love for God, on the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month. The place where they gathered is not mentioned, but it was most likely before the house of God, where the priests, the Levites and the books of the Holy Bible were.

9.0.1.en: They sanctified a fast on this day, a voluntary fast not prescribed by the Law of Moses. By this fast they drew near to God. We shall notice in the rest of this chapter that they thanked God and praised Him, and so joy was mingled with sorrow, as happened on the Feast of Trumpets, because holy sorrow in repentance gives peace, just as joy is also accompanied by inner peace. Even today sorrow is mingled with joy in the sacrament of confession, for repentance is accompanied by spiritual joy in God. Fasts, too, are always joined to prayers.

9.0.2.en: This fast was joined with humbling before God, for they put on sackcloth, which is coarse clothing, and put dust on their heads, remembering their sins; that is, they humbled themselves before God. Humbling in fasting makes it acceptable before God, as the prophet Isaiah said (Isa 58:5). In this voluntary fast, which the Law did not mention, we see a support for what the Apostles and the Fathers did when they appointed fasts which the Church keeps to this day, although Christ mentioned only the idea of fasting and Himself fasted for us. God gives us the idea of fasting and waits for us to respond to Him. This is what the Church did, appointing its various fasts throughout the year.

9.1.0.en: The second condition that Isaiah mentioned for an acceptable fast was fulfilled here by the people, namely breaking the bonds of evil. They separated themselves from the foreign women, as the Law prescribed; that is, they kept away from everything that bound them to idolatrous worship, that they might live in purity before God.

9.1.1.en: The book of Ezra (Ezra 9) tells us that Ezra was greatly distressed when he heard that the people had joined themselves to foreign women. Perhaps they had separated from them at that time, but afterward went back and joined themselves to them again; and here, when they fasted, they separated once more from these foreign women.

9.1.2.en: The third condition for an acceptable fast they fulfilled by their confession of their sins, and by this they obtained God's mercies, as David mentioned in (Ps 32:5) when he confessed his sin, and likewise Job when he confessed before all (Job 31:34). We notice here two kinds of confession: a common confession of the people before God, besides a personal confession before the priest, when the person laid his hand on the sacrifice and then the priest slew it on his behalf.

9.2.0.en: The fourth condition for an acceptable fast is the reading of the word of God, and they read in the book of the Law of the Lord, sitting quietly and listening to the word of God for a fourth part of the day, which is about three hours, since the day is about 12 hours, from six in the morning to six in the evening. Perhaps they would read a portion, and then the priests and Levites would explain it to the people, and there may have been an opportunity to answer the people's questions. It is also possible that they read to all, then divided them into groups, and then one of the Levites or priests sat down to explain to them according to their language and to answer their questions, as we mentioned in (ch. 8:8). It appears that the humbling of the people, their separation from the foreign wives and their confession of sin helped them to approach the word of God and to listen to it with attention.

9.2.1.en: Likewise the people's listening to the book of the Law at the Feast of Shouting, and then during the days of the Feast of Tabernacles, stirred their longing to ask to listen to the word of God.

9.2.2.en: The fifth condition for an acceptable fast is prayer, for the crowds assembled, after their reading in the Law, spent the second fourth of the day, about three hours, in glorifying God and bowing down to Him, that is, prayers of thanksgiving and praise to God joined with humility through prostrations (metanoias).

9.2.3.en: Listening to the word of God and meditating on it moves the heart to prayer, whether in thanksgiving and praise, or in humility and repentance.

9.2.4.en: The prayers of thanksgiving and glorification came from their sense of the mercy of God, who received them when they confessed their sins and humbled themselves before Him; for repentance increases by reading the word of God, and it moves the heart to thanksgiving and worship. Although it is mentioned that they spent a fourth of the day in reading and the second fourth in prayer, perhaps they repeated this, that is, they read in the third fourth and prayed in the fourth, so that they continued all day, twelve hours, in reading and prayer. This variety in the spiritual portions helped them not to grow weary, and therefore to enjoy being with God for a long time. This is what the children of God need to this day, whether those who worship God in the world, or in the wilderness, and also the solitaries.

9.2.5.en: God rejoices in your fasting and your drawing near to Him, so always join your fasting with humility, repentance, reading and prayer, and you will taste the sweetness of fellowship with God and rejoice in fasting. Your God has fasted on your behalf, and He must sit with you, so do not be slow to hasten to Him.

9.3.s.en: (2) Thanksgiving to God who rescued His people from Egypt and cared for them in the wilderness

9.3.0.en: Eight of the Levites stood upon the stairs, that is, a raised platform with steps, so as to be at a higher level than the people, so that they could easily be seen and heard at the time of prayer and the reading of the holy Scriptures. Perhaps this platform is the very one that they prepared and used on the Feast of Shouting, on which Ezra and thirteen of the priests stood (ch. 8:4), or perhaps it was another pulpit in the Temple.

9.3.1.en: When these Levites, among whom there may have been priests, stood, they prayed in a loud voice from their depths, so that the Holy Bible expressed it by saying that they “cried.”

9.3.2.en: These eight prayed on the pulpit, either all with one voice, or one after another in turn. It is also possible that they divided the assembled people into eight parts, and each of the Levites led a group of the people in prayer.

9.3.3.en: The number eight signifies eternity, for these Levites by their prayers lift up the hearts of the people to life with God and the Kingdom of Heaven.

9.4.0.en: As the Levites felt the warmth of prayer, they wished to share the people with them, so they called them to stand up and pray with them and bless God. This prayer is thanksgiving and praise.

9.4.1.en: The Levites asked the people to praise God, the Eternal, the Everlasting, because He is above all gods and all creatures.

9.5.0.en: The Levites declared (and the Septuagint translation says that the speaker was Ezra, the spiritual leader of the people), and in their glorification of God they proclaimed that He is the one God, the Creator of all beings in heaven and on earth. He is worthy of glorification by all, not because He is in need, but because this is the natural feeling of all His creatures, that they should glorify Him.

9.5.1.en: In this prayer they declared not only that He is the one God and the Creator of all, but also that He gives life to all creatures; He is the secret of their continuance, and therefore glorifying Him is a duty, because He is the secret of the life of all His creatures.

9.6.0.en: Ur of the Chaldees: a city situated in the south of Mesopotamia, in Iraq.

9.6.1.en: The prayer here began with thanking God for His works with His people, after they had glorified God, blessed by all His creation. In these two verses they blessed God for His choosing of Abram, the father of the people of God. This choosing is a free divine grace which God grants to those who love Him, for Abram worshiped God although idolatry was spread around him in the whole world.

9.6.2.en: Out of the love of God He brought Abram out from the midst of his people, who had begun to be defiled by idolatry, in order to keep him alone in the wilderness in the right faith.

9.6.3.en: And God's love added a new grace for Abram by changing his name to Abraham, so that he might feel the following:

9.6.4.en: 1- That he would live a new life to God in purity, better than his former life among his family.

9.6.5.en: 2- Abram means “exalted father,” while Abraham means “father of a great multitude.” The change of his name was thus good news to him that he would be the father of a great people who believe in God, the people of the children of Israel.

9.6.6.en: God also gave a grace to Abraham, namely the covenant which He made with him because of his faithfulness in the worship of God. He promised him that he would inherit and possess the whole land of Canaan, in which six idolatrous peoples dwelt. And God fulfilled His promise, for the seed of Abraham possessed this land in the days of Joshua.

9.6.7.en: God is true and faithful in fulfilling His promises, and human beings respond to Him according to their faith and love. Seldom is it said of a man that he is faithful, but faithfulness is mentioned of Moses and Abraham.

9.7.0.en: The Red Sea (Yam Suph): the Red Sea.

9.7.1.en: “Dealt proudly against them”: they did evil to them, that is, they wronged them.

9.7.2.en: “Thou didst divide the sea”: You split the sea.

9.7.3.en: After thanking God for His choosing of Abraham, they thank God for His care of His people the children of Israel, whom the Egyptians humbled. When they cried out to God, He sent them Moses and struck Egypt with great wonders, the ten plagues, by which He showed the weakness of their idolatrous gods, confirmed the faith of His people, and called the Egyptians to faith.

9.7.4.en: After the people of God had gone out of Egypt and reached the Red Sea, Pharaoh turned back and went out after them, to bring them back as slaves to him, to serve him in building cities and in every work. They cried out to God, and then He divided the Red Sea for them, which had been an obstacle to them in their flight, and made it a road through which they fled to the wilderness of Sinai. And the pillar of fire stood between them and the Egyptians and protected them.

9.7.5.en: When Pharaoh hardened his heart and followed the people of God into the sea, God brought His people out into the wilderness of Sinai and overwhelmed Pharaoh and all his army with water in the sea, so that they all died. God became a glorified name among all the peoples of the world, who heard of this great miracle, so all the peoples feared Him and some of them believed in Him, like Rahab.

9.7.6.en: The thanksgiving to God for delivering them from the Egyptians is remembered by the people now because God delivered them from the bondage of Babylon: He overthrew Babylon and the kingdom of the Medes and Persians took its place, which sent the people of God back to their land, and they built the Temple and Jerusalem and worshiped Him with joy.

9.7.7.en: The name of God was glorified through Pharaoh, and is glorified today through the building of the wall of Jerusalem, despite the obstinacy of the enemies.

9.8.0.en: After God delivered His people from the bondage of Egypt, they held fast to Him and asked His guidance in the vast wilderness of Sinai. So He sent them a pillar of cloud by day to overshadow them, which turned at night into a pillar of fire to give them light.

9.8.1.en: The pillar of cloud or the pillar of fire was not only a guide for the movements of the people of God, but a sign of the presence of God, which reassured them and made their hearts joyful, so they glorified God and blessed Him.

9.8.2.en: Perhaps the people's remembering God's guidance of them in the wilderness of Sinai was an incentive for them to seek God's guidance in their conduct and in their life with Him and with those around them, after He had reassured them by the building of the wall of Jerusalem.

9.8.3.en: It is good that you remember God's gifts and kindnesses and thank Him for them, for this shows your appreciation of God's love and urges you to enjoy His care more than before, so that your heart always rejoices.

9.9.0.en: God's love appeared in His spiritual care of His people. After He separated them from the idolatrous peoples, He Himself came down upon Mount Sinai and gave them His commandments and laws, that they might live by them. He also sanctified the Sabbath day that they might worship Him on it every week. They lived in these laws and commandments every day, every week and throughout the year, and by these good teachings they were distinguished from the rest of the idolatrous peoples of the world and enjoyed the presence of God in their midst. Moses was their spiritual leader, who received all these teachings from God in order to guide them in the straight way.

9.10.0.en: God also cared for their material needs. He gave them in a miraculous way food every day from heaven and also water from the rock wherever they went, so that they lacked nothing for forty years. God also promised them the inheritance of the land of Canaan, which overflows with many good things, after they should complete their journey in the wilderness of Sinai.

9.10.1.en: Thus we see complete care from God and inexpressible love, and thus His people lacked nothing. This is the love of God. But what, one wonders, was the people's reaction? Sadly it was bad, as we shall see in the following verses.

9.11.s.en: (3) The longsuffering of God toward His rebellious people

9.11.0.en: “Dealt proudly”: they wronged God, that is, they rebelled against Him.

9.11.1.en: “Hardened their necks”: when an animal stiffens its neck it refuses to submit to the work of drawing farm implements, and the phrase means rebellion.

9.11.2.en: The people's reaction was very strange, the very opposite of what was expected. Instead of thanking God and worshiping Him faithfully like Moses, they rebelled against God, refusing to submit to His commandments, and they also refused to listen to His Law and to the guidance of Moses to them, that they should return to God. In addition to that, they forgot God's wonders with them, whether in bringing them out of the land of Egypt or in caring for them in the wilderness of Sinai. And the hardest of all this was that they preferred bondage in Egypt to life with God, so they appointed a leader in place of Moses to lead them back to Egypt.

9.11.3.en: What is wonderful is God's longsuffering toward His people and His great mercy: He did not forsake them, but gave them an opportunity for repentance and led them about in the wilderness of Sinai, and when they were partly sorry for their sins, He forgave them and went on caring for them in the wilderness, because in truth He is a gracious and compassionate God.

9.12.0.en: Despite God's mercy, His people went back to rebelling against Him. While He was giving them the commandments and the Law and the pattern of the tabernacle of meeting, that He might dwell in their midst by the hand of Moses, they made a god for themselves, a golden calf, to worship instead of God, imitating the idolatrous nations around them.

9.13.0.en: In the face of all this rebellion and evil, God's mercy and care for His people in the wilderness continued. He led them by the pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night; that is, He remained present with them and their leader. God's spiritual care for His children continued: He did not withdraw from them His commandments and Law, but His Holy Spirit continued to guide them through these commandments and teachings by the hand of Moses, the priests, the Levites and the elders of the people (Num 11:24-25). God's care also continued in feeding them manna and giving them water from the rock.

9.13.1.en: We see here the people, who are praying on this day, repeating their thanksgiving to God for His care by the pillar of cloud and fire, the commandments, the manna and the water, because God's care was not affected by the evil of their fathers; rather, God remained good and faithful to His people despite all their rebellion.

9.13.2.en: The wonder also appeared in God's care when He preserved their clothes and their sandals for forty years in the wilderness, and also preserved their feet, so that they did not swell from much walking in the desert.

9.14.0.en: During their journey in the wilderness they met peoples east of the Dead Sea, before they crossed the Jordan and entered the land of Canaan. They triumphed over them by the power of God and possessed their land; these were Sihon and Og, the great kings, kings of the Amorites.

9.14.1.en: Thus the power of God is made manifest, who worked with His people, who were shepherds of sheep untrained for war. They triumphed over strong kings and scattered in many directions to possess wide lands east of the river Jordan, such as Heshbon and Bashan, under the leadership of Moses the prophet, before their entering the land of Canaan.

9.15.0.en: In God's care for His people, He multiplied their children, preserved their lives and gave them strength, so that they were able to enter the land of Canaan and seize its fortified cities, such as Jericho, and possess its wide lands full of good things. It was planted with vineyards and full of wells that gave water abundantly (Deut 9:3, Deut 7:24; Josh 11:12, 17; Judg 1:4). So Your people enjoyed abundant delights which You gave them, for which they had not labored in planting and building.

9.16.0.en: Sadly the fathers did not thank God for all these many gifts, but disobeyed His commandments and left His Law, and when God sent prophets to them to bring them back to Him, they rejected the word of God and rose up against the prophets and killed them, like Isaiah, whom they sawed in two with a wooden saw, and Jeremiah, whom they stoned (Heb 11:37).

9.17.0.en: After the people of God had possessed the land of Canaan in the days of Joshua, they went back and left the commandments of God and entered into idolatrous marriages, so the Gentiles ruled over them and humbled them, and then they cried out to God, and He sent them saviors, the judges, such as Gideon, Jephthah and Samson, who delivered them from their oppressors and brought them back to the worship of God. This shows God's longsuffering, mercies and tenderness toward His people, whom, however much they sinned and returned to Him, He receives and saves. This is especially so since they repeated their disobedience many times: whenever their enemies humbled them and they cried out to God, He delivered them, but they returned again to their negligence and disobedience, so their enemies humbled them, and they cried out to God, who delivered them. Thus God's mercies intervened many times to rescue His disobedient people.

9.18.0.en: The people of God continued in their sins and their attachment to idolatrous worship, which compelled God to discipline them with the Assyrian captivity and then the Babylonian captivity, that they might repent and return to Him. Thus God's mercies kept seeking His people, by severity and by gentleness, that they might live with Him.

9.18.1.en: Throughout these periods of disobedience God never tired of sending His prophets to warn His people and rebuke them for their sins. These are the countless mercies of God, who desires the salvation of His children.

9.18.2.en: God did not deal with His people according to their sins, but bore with them and gave them successive opportunities for repentance. The continuance of His people rests on His divine mercy, for He does not wish to destroy His people as a just punishment for their sins, but wishes them to live with Him, that He may delight them with His blessings.

9.18.3.en: God's commandments and Law guarantee His children a noble life and joy with God, but leaving them is what exposes them to humiliation and bondage.

9.19.s.en: (4) Confession of sin and making a covenant

9.19.0.en: After the prayer reviewed the mercies of God in the face of the people's disobedience, it now asks the great and awesome God, before whom the hearts of His children are humbled, to look with His tenderness upon His people, who are now humbled in bondage under the hand of the Gentiles, namely Assyria, Babylon, Media and Persia. God had given them the land of Canaan, full of good things, but because of their sins they have come into the humiliation of bondage, dwelling in it, and they have no hope except God, their gracious God, who is able to keep them. Thus feelings of the fear of God are mingled with hope, for He is at once the awesome and the gracious God, in whom His people hope.

9.19.1.en: This prayer shows the people's confession of their sins, themselves, their fathers and their kings, and their acknowledgment of the grace of God, His mercies and His longsuffering. It is a contrite prayer that calls forth the mercies of God.

9.19.2.en: At the end of the prayer the people show the extent of the distress they suffer and that they do not benefit from the good things of the land, for these go to the kings while they are in hard bondage, scarcely obtaining their food, and all the good things go to the king, so their bodies have become humbled like those of slaves.

9.20.0.en: The prayer ended with a definite positive act, namely the making of a covenant with God, which all the people declared and the priests and Levites, that is, the spiritual leaders of the people, confirmed. It is understood implicitly that this covenant included holding fast to the commandments and Law of God and keeping away from idolatrous worship and all evil.

9.20.1.en: To confirm the covenant, the people wrote it down so that it might be a witness against them and a declaration that they did not wish to turn back from it by their free will. Then a number of the priests and Levites came forward and sealed this written covenant, as a declaration on their part that they were responsible for carrying out this covenant and for always urging the people to hold fast to it. Thus we see that the long prayer before had a strong effect in making a firm and lasting covenant with God. By this the prophecy of Jeremiah was fulfilled that the people of God after the captivity would “join themselves to the LORD in a perpetual covenant that shall not be forgotten” (Jer 50:5).

9.20.2.en: May you turn your spiritual feelings into definite exercises that help you in life with God, so that you strive in the spiritual way by rejecting the beloved sin and holding fast to the spiritual practices that bring you near to God, such as prayer, fasting and reading the Holy Bible, and from them result your love and service to God. Renewal of the covenant
